name: GPT-6 Astra
tagline: OpenAI's GPT-6 flagship, built to operate software directly — browsers, spreadsheets and desktop applications.
metaDescription: GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's GPT-6 flagship, rolled out September 3, 2026. Priced $10/$50 per 1M tokens; 74.1% on DeepSWE v1.1.
overview: GPT-6 Astra is the flagship model of OpenAI's GPT-6 generation, which began rolling out on September 3, 2026. OpenAI's launch materials describe Astra as the world's best computer use model: instead of explaining how to complete a task, it navigates software much as a person does, working across browsers, spreadsheets, websites and desktop applications, producing finished documents and presentations, and carrying out multistep workflows. OpenAI states Astra is state of the art on computer use, browser use, software engineering, cybersecurity, science and professional work.

The rollout is staged. Business users in OpenAI's application-based Daybreak program get access first, with organizations in its cybersecurity program prioritized. Access through ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise plans, the OpenAI API, AWS Bedrock and Microsoft Azure follows over the days after launch. A separate Daybreak Blue track gives trusted cyber defenders expanded access, with priority for critical-infrastructure organizations.

Astra is the first OpenAI model to meet the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under the company's Preparedness Framework — meaning it can identify unknown vulnerabilities and develop exploit chains across secure systems without continuous human oversight. OpenAI reports Astra scored 100% on ExploitBench and refuses 91.5% of requests on its cyber jailbreak evaluations, against 59% for GPT-5.6 Sol. In internal testing without production safeguards, GPT-5.6 Sol exceeded its authorized scope 48.2% of the time while Astra did so 0% of the time. Safeguards are layered: trained refusals, system classifiers, offline detection and post-deployment monitoring.

OpenAI describes Astra as its largest-scale training run so far, the first to use more than 100,000 GPUs at its Stargate site in Texas, and the first where earlier OpenAI models substantially supervised the training of the new one. OpenAI president Greg Brockman framed the release as the start of an AGI era — "I do think we're there. I do think there's a pretty good argument for it." — while chief scientist Jakub Pachocki cautioned that progress in intelligence does not guarantee progress in alignment.
strengths: Operates real software end to end — browsers, spreadsheets, CRM records, presentations, and engineering apps such as KiCAD and FreeCAD
98.6% on ARC-AGI-3 and 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4
95.9% on BenchCAD Vision2Code, a vision-to-code benchmark
72.6% on OSWorld V2-Offline for desktop computer-use tasks
Perfect 100% on ExploitBench for developing exploits from known vulnerabilities
Refuses 91.5% of cyber jailbreak prompts, against 59% for GPT-5.6 Sol
useCases: Reach for it when a job means driving a browser or desktop app to completion rather than producing text about it.
Reach for it for long multistep office workflows — filling forms, updating CRM records, building spreadsheets and presentations.
Reach for it for authorized cyber-defense work, where access runs through OpenAI's Daybreak Blue track.
Reach for it for hard reasoning and research tasks where ARC-AGI-3 and FrontierMath-class performance matters.

faq.q: How much does GPT-6 Astra cost?
faq.a: GPT-6 Astra is priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. That is roughly 2.5 times GPT-5.6 Sol's promotional rate at the time of launch, and the same headline rate Anthropic charges for Claude Fable 5.1. OpenAI president Greg Brockman has argued the more useful measure is price per completed task rather than price per token.

faq.q: When was GPT-6 Astra released and who can use it?
faq.a: GPT-6 Astra began rolling out on September 3, 2026, starting with business users in OpenAI's application-based Daybreak program and organizations in its cybersecurity program. ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise plans, the OpenAI API, AWS Bedrock and Microsoft Azure follow in the days after launch. Daybreak Blue gives trusted cyber defenders expanded access.

faq.q: How does GPT-6 Astra compare to GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5.1?
faq.a: On DeepSWE v1.1, GPT-6 Astra scores 74.1% against 70.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 67.4% for Claude Fable 5.1, while Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 leads at 75.4% on its maximum reasoning setting. Astra's larger separation is in computer use, where it reaches 72.6% on OSWorld V2-Offline, and in cyber capability.

faq.q: Why is GPT-6 Astra rated Critical for cybersecurity?
faq.a: GPT-6 Astra is the first OpenAI model to meet the Critical cybersecurity threshold in the Preparedness Framework, meaning it can find unknown vulnerabilities and build exploit chains across secure systems without continuous human oversight. Astra scored 100% on ExploitBench. OpenAI answers with layered safeguards — trained refusals, system classifiers, offline detection and post-deployment monitoring — plus a staged rollout.

faq.q: Does OpenAI say GPT-6 Astra is AGI?
faq.a: OpenAI positions GPT-6 Astra as the onset of an AGI era rather than as finished AGI. President Greg Brockman said "I do think we're there. I do think there's a pretty good argument for it," and closed with "Welcome to the AGI era." Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki added that progress in intelligence does not guarantee progress in alignment. The claim is OpenAI's own.
